items.title: 5th Circuit strikes down No Surprises billing benchmark in win for providers
items.reason: This item reports a regulatory/judicial ruling (5th Circuit court decision) that directly impacts payer reimbursement practices and enforcement of No Surprises Act billing benchmarks, a core payer litigation and enforcement matter.
items.summary: The 5th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that insurers cannot use ghost rates or exclude bonus payments when calculating the qualifying payment amount (QPA) benchmark under the No Surprises Act, which determines reimbursement for out-of-network claims. This decision is expected to increase payouts to providers for out-of-network services by requiring insurers to use more complete billing data in their benchmark calculations. The ruling represents a win for providers in litigation over payer methodologies for calculating surprise billing reimbursement obligations and affects how insurers must comply with federal surprise billing protections.
